And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Prabhat Kumar Ojha Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Arvind Kumar Shukla,Mohd. Nafees Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Arvind Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Devesh Kumar, learned AGA for the State through video conferencing.

2. The present application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in Case Crime No.0081 of 2024, under Sections 376, 354, 328, 120B IPC and Section 67 of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station- Maheshganj District- Pratapgarh.
3. Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that he has been falsely implicated along with entire family.
Correct fact is that the first informant was a consenting party as both of them are in relationship for more than four years.
It is further submitted that co-accused Akhil Pandey has already been enlarged on anticipatory bail by this Court in Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory
Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.PC. No.1361 of 2024 dated 24.06.2024

.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant submits that there is specific allegation against the applicant for committing rape and blackmailing her on the basis of some obscene video of first informant.
He further submitted that in view of the seriousness of the allegations made against the applicant, he is not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusal of record, it appears that there is serious allegation against the applicant for committing rape with the first informant and also blackmailing her on the basis of obscene video.

So far as anticipatory bail granted to co-accused Akhil Pandey is concerned, the applicant cannot claim parity with co-accused Akhil Pandey because there was no specific allegation against the co-accused Akhil Pandey but specific allegation is against the present applicant.
Therefore, this Court does not find it a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
6. In view of above, the present anticipatory bail application is rejected.
